item.title: Warriors’ Brandin Podziemski flexes a sweet but unexpected ride to Heat game
item.description: Isaiah J. Downing-Imagn Images Warriors’ Brandin Podziemski flexes a sweet but unexpected ride to Heat game appeared first on ClutchPoints . Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here . Brandin Podziemski and the Golden State Warriors are set to host the Miami Heat on Thursday night, and the young guard made sure his arrival at Chase Center did not go unnoticed . The NBA shared a clip of Podziemski rolling into the arena’s underground parking garage on an electric scooter . The 23-year-old kept it casual for the ride, rocking a black beanie, a puffer jacket over a gray hoodie and a pair of red patterned pants as he cruised past the Warriors’ signage. Brandin Podziemski slides in on the scooter ahead of Warriors-Heat 😅🛴 Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) (via @NBA ) pic.twitter.com/2wicdNvS4k — ClutchPoints (@ClutchPoints) November 6, 2026 It was certainly not the kind of entrance fans are used to seeing from an NBA player, especially one who just landed a big payday. Podziemski agreed to a five-year, $110 million rookie-scale extension with Golden State in October, a deal that includes a mutual option in the fifth year and a trade kicker. He later thanked the organization for taking a “leap with faith” on him . Podziemski, the 19th overall pick in the 2023 NBA Draft, is now in his fourth season with the Warriors. Podziemski’s season did not get off to the smoothest start. He was ruled out of the season opener against the Los Angeles Lakers with lower back soreness. Since returning, though, he has been a key part of a Warriors team that has caught fire. Golden State has won five straight games after dropping its first three, improving to 5-3 on the season. Podziemski chipped in 20 points on 7-of-15 shooting, including 3-of-8 from deep, in Monday’s 116-113 win over the Phoenix Suns. Stephen Curry led the way with 34 points in that one, while rookie Yaxel Lendeborg added 16 points and five assists. The Warriors will now look to extend their winning streak against a Heat team playing on the second night of a back-to-back. Miami is 3-5 on the season but is coming off a thrilling 117-116 overtime win over the LA Clippers on Wednesday, thanks to a go-ahead 3-pointer from former Warriors star Klay Thompson . Thompson, who won four championships in Golden State, is making his first trip back to Chase Center as a member of the Heat . Andrew Wiggins, another former Warrior, is also on Miami’s roster. Podziemski will hope his performance on the court is as smooth as his ride to the arena. item.description: Three Monroe County Region volleyball teams are moving on. Bedford, Flat Rock and St. Mary Catholic Central captured district championships on Thursday, Nov. 5. They will continue their quests for state championships in regional action on Tuesday, Nov. 10. Ida, New Boston Huron and Erie Mason saw their seasons come to an end. More: Updated District volleyball pairings A roundup of all the district finals follows. Division 2 at Airport CARLETON – A dominant third set showed Flat Rock’s vast potential. The defending state runners-up got the job done in the first two sets, then hit their stride in the third set of a 25-15, 25-19, 25-11 victory over New Boston Huron. “The first set we had a good hitting percentage but weren’t good on serve receive,” Flat Rock coach Morgan Delhey said. “In the second we were good on serve receive but didn’t hit for a high percentage. We put it all together in the third.” Flat Rock’s dynamic 1-2 punch at the net Sarah Giroux and Lily Klein dominated the final set with five kills apiece. Klein had four putaways in one streak of five straight points with Giroux notching the other. Giroux finished with 17 kills and 7 digs while Klein recorded 11 kills and 4 blocks. Taylor Hesse contributed 7 kills, Zoe Ryan 26 assists and 13 digs and Elle Dwyer 6 digs for the 25-11-1 Rams. “Tonight we found a way to keep our momentum, keeping excited even when we had a big lead,” Delhey said. Flat Rock advances to regional play at Dearborn Divine Child at 6:30 p.m. on Tuesday, Nov. 10. item.title: Zuffa Boxing 12 Returns to England Saturday
item.description: What to Know Zuffa Boxing 12 returns to the Copper Box Arena in London for its fourth UK card on Saturday, November 7. British cruiserweights Chris Billam-Smith and Chev Clarked headline Zuffa Boxing 12. American Shane Mosley Jr. crosses the pond to face Denzel Bentley in the middleweight division, joined by Florida’s heavyweight prospect Da’Mazion Vanhouter. The Zuffa Boxing 12 card airs on Paramount+ with prelims at 12 p.m. ET / 9 a.m. PT, and the main card at 2 p.m. ET / 11 a.m. PT. Zuffa Boxing staged its first six cards after its launch at the Meta Apex in Las Vegas, a small venue and a reasonable choice as the promotion settled into its new venture. Since then, four of its six numbered cards, including Saturday’s event, have taken place in Great Britain. Zuffa Boxing 12 is getting comfortable at the Copper Box Arena in London, returning for its second straight card there in London on Saturday. While the card is loaded with British talent for home fans, two Americans and a U.S.-based Austrian are worth watching. Billam-Smith vs Clarke: A Rematch Ten Years In The Making Former amateur foes Chris Billam-Smith and Chev Clarke will see how things look ten years later. Photo: Zuffa Boxing Former light heavyweight champion Chris Billam-Smith (22-2, 14 KOs) has a score to settle in a rematch with British Olympian Chev Clarke (12-2, 9 KOs). The pair met for the British amateur championship ten years ago, with Clarke getting the better of Billam-Smith. “Me and Chev competing for the amateur elite national final title that means so much to all the amateur fighters. I think it’s like the equivalent of the Golden Gloves in the States, so it’s a fight I really, really wanted to win, and really thought I would,” recalls Billam-Smith. “But he got the nod that day, and that helps add a little bit of spice to this fight because the 36-year-old me now gets to do 26-year-old me a favor and show him how much I’ve improved over the years and basically get one back for younger me.” Billam-Smith is coming off a bruising fight against Ryan Rosicki of Canada , with both showing their grit before Rosicki’s corner pulled their man out after the seventh round. Clarke showed his own kind of grit in his last fight. He had to climb up off the canvas twice before eventually stopping former world title challenger Jack Massey with a crowd-pleasing knockout win. Clarke doesn’t think their fight a decade ago will influence Saturday’s rematch, as both are different competitors today. “I think we’re different human beings now,” Clarke said. “He’s a dad. item.title: 'We grew today': Newcomer Colleen Phiri sparks Holy Cross comeback
item.description: WORCESTER – The Holy Cross women’s basketball team graduated four starters from last year’s Patriot League champion and NCAA Tournament team. Their loss was substantial in terms of leadership and production. Still, the Crusaders, and coach Candice Green, believed they had the talent and the determination to keep their predecessors’ standard of success going in 2026-27. Holy Cross proved that in its 10-point win at Boston College to start the season, and again in its comeback victory over Dartmouth in its home opener Nov. 5 at the Hart Center. Sophomore guard Colleen Phiri drove for the go-ahead layup with 1:30 left and made 1-2 free throws with 16 seconds to go and the Crusaders overcame a tough shooting night to beat the Big Green, 49-46. “I’m happy with our group,” Green said. “We grew today.” Holy Cross trailed by as many as nine and by seven at the end of the third quarter. HC scored the first six points of the fourth and held Dartmouth to seven points over the final 10 minutes. Phiri and sophomore guard Brianna McDermott sank big 3-pointers, and Phiri was clutch down the stretch. “It shows our resilience,” said Phiri, who also had a key defensive rebound with 35 seconds left. “It’s only Game 2, but this is what we’ve been practice for since the summer. We’ve been building for moments like this.” Phiri, who transferred to HC from George Washington, scored a game-high 21 points and had eight rebounds. As she has shown, she can shoot from 3 and take it to the rim. She scored 11 points in her Holy Cross debut at BC. “Everyone has been super welcoming,” Phiri said. “I love my teammates and my coaches. They make it feel like home.” Phiri’s tie-breaking layup gave Holy Cross its first lead since 7-5 in the first quarter. “I was thinking, ‘Just go,’” Phiri said of the decisive basket. “I felt all game like head of steam and momentum, and my teammates were encouraging me so I said, ‘I’m going to take this,’ and it went in.” Holy Cross shot just 32% from the field, but the Crusaders held Dartmouth to 26%. “I was happy with shots we were getting,” Green said. “They just weren’t falling. That’s why we play defense because you can’t control if ball goes in, but you can control the shots we give up. That’s what we focused on.” Dartmouth went 10-17 (1-13 Ivy League) last year. Brissett is going through the 11th season of his NFL career, his first with the Ravens. He started the 2026 campaign with the Cardinals, starting in the first eight games before the team benched him for Gardner Minshew. Demoting him down to QB3, Arizona ultimately decided to send him to Baltimore this week. Brissett enters an intriguing situation with his new chapter in Baltimore. The Ravens are dealing with injuries at quarterback, seeing Lamar Jackson on injured reserve and Tyler Huntley being out for the season. NFL insider Ian Rapoport provided his thoughts on Brissett’s status, seeing him to be on pace to be the starter in Week 10. If he comes over at about $5 million, a little more in salary, the Arizona Cardinals and the Ravens will basically split that. item.title: Pistons Trade Idea Would Land Rising NBA Star in Potential Championship Move
item.description: The Detroit Pistons have already established themselves as one of the Eastern Conference’s most dangerous teams, but an intriguing new trade idea could give president of basketball operations Trajan Langdon something significant to consider. What if Detroit could add another 20-point scorer who also happens to be an outstanding perimeter defender? That’s the possibility surrounding Nickeil Alexander-Walker , the Atlanta Hawks guard who has developed into one of the NBA’s most productive two-way players. And while acquiring him could require a substantial investment, the potential fit alongside Cade Cunningham is difficult to ignore. Oct 16, 2026; Dallas, Texas, USA; Atlanta Hawks guard Nickeil Alexander-Walker (7) reacts during the game between the Mavericks and the Hawks at American Airlines Center. Mandatory Credit: Jerome Miron-Imagn Images Credit: IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect (Reuters) Pistons Trade Idea Could Bring Nickeil Alexander-Walker to Detroit A November 5 trade analysis raised the possibility of Detroit pursuing Alexander-Walker , suggesting the Pistons could consider an aggressive move similar to the New York Knicks’ acquisition of Mikal Bridges. The reasoning is straightforward. Detroit has a championship-caliber foundation, but adding an established scorer who can defend opposing guards and wings could make that foundation even stronger. Alexander-Walker, 28, is coming off a breakout 2025-26 season in which he averaged 20.8 points, 3.4 rebounds, and 3.7 assists. He has carried that momentum into the new season. Through nine games, Alexander-Walker is averaging approximately 21.7 points while shooting better than 40 percent from three-point range. item.description: IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect The Toronto Blue Jays have some work to do to improve an offense that ranked dead last in baseball in home runs in 2026. ESPN’s Buster Olney, appearing on First Up , pegs the Blue Jays as a favorite to land Sato. He’d be joining his countryman, Kazuma Okamoto, in Toronto. Teruaki Sato is a hitter who, folks with other teams tell me, the Blue Jays are going to be in big… He’s a high-impact guy. Fellow insider Steve Phillips, however, told the guys on First Up that because third base is his main position, there isn’t a natural spot, as Okamoto is set there. Pavel Zacha (5) scored twice, while Mark Kastelic (3), Elias Lindholm (6), Morgan Geekie (4), and Fraser Minten (6) each added one. Michael DiPietro made 16 saves in his fourth straight win. Old friend Justin Brazeau , in just his second game of the season, opened the scoring at the 9:04 mark. Hendrix Lapierre set up Brazeau in the right circle, and on the Penguins’ first shot of the game, Brazeau beat DiPietro high blocker side . The Bruins responded just three minutes later. Pavel Zacha, JJ Peterka , and David Pastrnak were moving around in the offensive zone. Peterka played an airborne puck through his legs to Pastrnak in the left circle. Pastrnak played a cross-crease pass to Zacha, and he beat Arturs Silovs high to tie the game. Frederic Brunet , who missed the last three games as a healthy scratch, steered a shot on goal. The fourth line created traffic in front of Silovs, and Mark Kastelic redirected Brunet’s shot past Silovs to make it 2-1. Erik Karlsson coughed up the puck in the Penguins’ defensive zone, and Elias Lindholm pounced on it. He redirected a shot from Kaedan Korczak behind DiPietro at the 7:57 mark . The Bruins reclaimed their two-goal lead in the back half of the second period. David Pastrnak played the puck to JJ Peterka, who moved in with Pavel Zacha on a 2-on-1. Peterka backhanded a pass to Zacha, and he beat Silovs high for his second of the night. item.description: After a much-needed bye week, the Kentucky Wildcats return to action on Saturday, heading down to Knoxville to take on the Tennessee Volunteers in not just a rivalry game, but a game with College Football Playoff implications. The Volunteers are coming off a bye week as well, following a 27-24 loss to South Carolina in Columbia. Tennessee enters the matchup at 6-2, with its only other loss coming by three points against Texas. This isn’t quite the same Tennessee team Kentucky has grown accustomed to facing under Josh Heupel. This Volunteer team’s identity is built on a top-15-ranked defense, while an offense that has typically been the program’s calling card ranks just outside the top 60 nationally but does have a dominant ground game, led by Heisman candidate DeSean Bishop. This will be the third time the two programs have met as top-20 teams, and just the second in the modern era. 2022: No. 3 Tennessee 44, No. 19 Kentucky 6 1951: No. 1 Tennessee 28, No. 9 Kentucky 0 1950: No. 9 Tennessee 7, No. 3 Kentucky 0 Will Stein is doing his part to put the “Old Kentucky Football” mantra behind the program. Will he continue to do so by coaching Kentucky to a win at Neyland Stadium for just the second time since 1984? Let’s take a look at the matchup. Run Game Kentucky and Tennessee both have good run games, both ranking in the top ten nationally in rushing offense success. That said, the Volunteers rely much more heavily on the ground game, averaging 213 rushing yards per game (second in the SEC) and running the ball on 63% of their offensive plays. In comparison, Kentucky averages 163 rushing yards per game and runs on 54.5% of its offensive plays. Defensively, they rank just a couple of spots apart in stopping the run. Tennessee allows 123 rushing yards per game, while the Wildcats allow 113.2. With the run game playing such an integral part for each team, it will be the largest offensive factor on Saturday. It is important for the Wildcats to establish the run to create opportunities through the air and consistently create manageable down-and-distance situations. At the same time, they have to limit Tennessee’s running attack, led by Bishop, who enters Saturday with 957 rushing yards and 11 touchdowns. “They’re running the ball as good as anybody for sure,” Stein said on Tuesday. Kentucky’s had some solid defensive performances vs. opposing running backs, but this unit has yet to face anyone like Bishop, who can absolutely carry this Vols offense to victory if the Wildcats don’t wrap up and maintain gap integrity. item.description: PITTSBURGH — On paper, Thursday night’s game at PPG Paints Arena between the Pittsburgh Penguins (5-9-2) and Boston Bruins (12-4-1) looked lopsided in Boston’s favor, and that is exactly how it played out in a 6-2 Bruins win. The Penguins made mistake after mistake in a listless effort, and the Bruins were more than happy to capitalize on many of them. The first period started off well enough for the Penguins. They killed a Bruins power play and grabbed a 1-0 lead midway through the period, but the wheels fell off after that. The Bruins scored three unanswered goals in less than seven minutes to close out the first. It was less what the Bruins were doing to the Penguins than the mistakes Pittsburgh made on its own, including seven first-period giveaways, several of which Boston turned into goals. The second period followed a similar script. The Penguins scored the first goal of the frame, but the Bruins got the next two and dominated play. Pittsburgh committed five more giveaways, and by the end of the period Erik Karlsson was a minus-4. In what was a microcosm of the poor decisions the Penguins made all night, down by three in the waning seconds of the period, Rickard Rakell inexplicably passed up a glorious scoring chance and instead tried a shot-pass to Sidney Crosby that didn’t come close to connecting, much to the chagrin of the PPG Paints Arena crowd. The third period was simply a lost cause. The Penguins gave up another goal, squandered an embarrassing two-on-none, and generally looked like they were skating in mud. The Penguins have now lost four consecutive games and remain stuck at 12 points, mired at the bottom of the Eastern Conference standings. Things don’t get any easier as they embark on a three-game California road trip through Los Angeles, Anaheim, and San Jose. item.title: Steve Young Makes Strong Statement on San Francisco 49ers Amid Injury Concerns
item.description: SANTA CLARA, CALIFORNIA - JANUARY 03: Former quarterback Steve Young of the San Francisco 49ers looks on prior to a game against the Seattle Seahawks at Levi's Stadium on January 03, 2026 in Santa Clara, California. (Photo by Lachlan Cunningham/Getty Images) Getty There is no question that the San Francisco 49ers have consistently dealt with injuries over the last few years. And while they enter Week 9 with a 6-1 record, injuries remain a major concern this season. Several players are currently sidelined, and while it’s not time to sound the alarm, the 49ers face a daunting task if they hope to reach their Super Bowl goal without their best players on the field and relatively healthy. Steve Young Addresses Injury Concerns Appearing on KNBR this week, 49ers legend and NFL Hall of Famer Steve Young discussed the team’s current state. He acknowledged that San Francisco can hang with anybody when healthy but emphasized that health remains a big “if.” “It’s like the if, if, if. We have Hall of Famers on both sides of the ball. We have a quarterback, we have a genius coach. We’re that team. But if we can’t keep people healthy, if we’re always mixing and matching, especially with our age, we’re really counting on Christian to carry such a big load, along with George. We’re asking a lot,” said Young. “And if those guys answer that call, we’re in the thick of it. No question. I just pray we quit talking about injuries and get the superstars out there consistently for the next 12 games. That’s what we need.” Steve Young knows what this team can be. Like every 49ers fan, he’s tired of waiting for a healthy roster. “I pray we can quit talking about injuries, and get the superstars on our team out there and consistent for the next twelve games.” (via Dirty Work w/ @Adamcopes & @dpapapops) — KNBR (@KNBR) November 5, 2026 49ers’ Current Injuries San Francisco is set to enter Sunday’s matchup against the Las Vegas Raiders with veteran wide receivers Mike Evans and Deebo Samuel both expected to miss the game, according to general manager John Lynch. Outside of those two, the team still has several players on IR and is also monitoring what appears to be a minor hamstring strain for running back Christian McCaffrey. Fortunately, the 49ers appear set to welcome back star pass rusher Nick Bosa and veteran WR DeMarcus Robinson from IR for Sunday’s game. That’s a positive sign as San Francisco continues to get a little healthier each day. item.description: The Detroit Tigers may have finished the 2026 season with a disappointing 76-86 record, but manager A.J. Hinch believes the organization has found something special in Kevin McGonigle. And his latest comments leave little doubt about just how important the young infielder will be to Detroit’s future. Following McGonigle’s selection as the 2026 Tiger of the Year , Hinch made a powerful declaration about the direction of the franchise. Not only does he view McGonigle as a cornerstone player, but he also believes Detroit needs more players who approach the game the same way. Detroit Tigers third baseman Kevin McGonigle (7) bats against Pittsburgh Pirates during the fourth inning at Comerica Park in Detroit on Friday, Sept. 25, 2026. Credit: USA TODAY Network via Reuters Connect (Reuters) A.J. Hinch Makes Bold Statement About Kevin McGonigle McGonigle was named Tiger of the Year on Wednesday by the Detroit chapter of the Baseball Writers’ Association of America, adding another honor to an incredible debut season. But perhaps the biggest takeaway from the announcement was Hinch’s assessment of what McGonigle means to the organization. “We’re going to build around him,” Hinch said in comments highlighted following Wednesday’s award announcement . Hinch explained that Detroit needs more players who possess McGonigle’s characteristics to move the organization forward. He also praised the young infielder’s outstanding all-around approach and expressed hope that McGonigle appreciates what he accomplished in his first major league season. That’s a pretty significant endorsement from a manager who has seen plenty of talented players throughout his career. And considering what McGonigle accomplished as a 22-year-old rookie, it’s not difficult to understand why Hinch feels that way. He received an overwhelming 21 of 23 first-place votes , while Greene and catcher Dillon Dingler collected the remaining support. Even more impressive, McGonigle became the first middle infielder to receive the award since Carlos Guillén in 2006. His numbers certainly justified the recognition. McGonigle finished the season batting .278 with 18 home runs, 72 RBIs, 97 runs scored, 95 walks and an .806 OPS. His 7.1 Baseball-Reference WAR led the entire American League , not just fellow rookies. He also became the first MLB rookie since Ted Williams in 1939 to reach at least 97 runs, 28 doubles, 18 home runs, 72 RBIs and 95 walks in a single season. item.description: 🎥 Cruzeiro rally past Bahia in chaos, sit pretty for Libertadores It was an ACTION-PACKED game at the Mineirão. Cruzeiro came out on top against Bahia on Thursday night (5). The Fox conceded a stunning goal, saw Fagner miss an unbelievable chance and even watched Kaio Jorge take center stage in a bizarre moment before shining once again. The Tricolor refused to give up. But Cruzeiro secured a 3–2 win in front of their home fans. And put themselves in a strong position to qualify for the 2027 Libertadores. Wonder goal or goalkeeping error? Cruzeiro fans had cause for concern just four minutes in when Fabrício Bruno had to be substituted with a suspected injury. Viña came off the bench to fill in. Then came Kike Olivera's superb goal. He had already tested Otávio in the 10th minute. And he made the breakthrough in the 31st. A nutmeg on Zé Lucas, followed by a finish that caught Otávio off guard. 🤯 Oh no, Fagner... Cruzeiro's first big chance of the game came in the 37th minute. But Fagner, completely unmarked, hit the crossbar. KJ levels before the break Kaio Jorge had barely been involved up to that point. But he was decisive when he found room to make a difference. He played a one-two with Arroyo and benefited from Ronaldo's error to get on the scoresheet. A slip, a Cruzeiro comeback and a WONDER GOAL VAR flagged a penalty for a foul on Viña. Kaio Jorge had the chance to celebrate again, but his standing foot let him down. And he blazed his penalty over. But Cruzeiro had Bruno Rodrigues. And he scored in the 69th minute after being honored for making 100 appearances for the club. Kaio Jorge redeemed himself in some style in the 86th minute. He brushed past Marcos Victor to score a superb goal. Rogério Ceni's side were rocked, but managed to get back into the game as Alejo ended his goal drought in the fifth minute of stoppage time. But the victory belonged to Cruzeiro. 📊 The standings Third-placed Cruzeiro moved up to 60 points. They opened up a seven-point gap over Bahia, who sit sixth. A Libertadores berth, whether direct or via the qualifying rounds, is within reach. Neither team will play again until Wednesday the 18th. Cruzeiro will host second-placed Palmeiras. item.title: Flyers Collapse Late in Thursday Loss vs. Rangers
item.description: NEW YORK – The Philadelphia Flyers (4-10-4) collapsed late vs. the New York Rangers (9-7-1) on Thursday at Madison Square Garden, giving the Rangers their first comeback win of the season and a devastating loss for the Flyers. Gabe Perrault, Pavel Dorofeyev, and Tye Kartye scored for the Rangers. Simon Benoit and Noel Acciari scored for the Flyers. It was all Rangers at the start of the game. Their forecheck was smothering the Flyers. They were maintaining possession of the puck and really putting the pressure on the Flyers. Philly was having a hard time breaking out of the defensive zone, and eventually, it would come back to haunt them. A blast from the blue line found J.T. Miller ’s stick in the slot, redirecting the puck to Gabe Perrault and past Joseph Woll and in for the early score, putting the Rangers up 1-0 over the Flyers in the first period. The Rangers kept the good chances coming. With less than 5 minutes to play in the period, New York nearly tacked on another, but Woll made a great pad save on Tye Kartye to keep it a 1-0 game. Philly put forward a better effort in the second half of the first period, but were still not creating enough, if any, high-danger chances. Despite going into the first intermission leading the shot battle 9-8, it was a very underwhelming first period for the Flyers. It felt like Rangers domination after the first 20 minutes, but it was only a 1-0 game. Early in the 2nd period, the Rangers nearly took the 2-0 lead, but Simon Benoit made an incredible stop with his stick to stop the puck from crossing the goal line, keeping the Flyers within one. Benoit then kept his best period as a Flyer going, scoring his first goal as a Flyer right around the halfway mark of the game, tying it up at 1. Noel Acciari then gave the Flyers the lead in the second period following a great pass from Denver Barkey , setting Acciari up for the easy score. Just as everyone thought, Benoit and Acciari gave the Flyers their first lead of the game. Each team had a power-play opportunity before the period came to an end, but neither was able to cash in. That brought the game to the second intermission with the Flyers up 2-1, but the Rangers leading in shots 18-17. The third period was very slow-moving, especially compared to the first two. There was not much going on in the first 10 minutes, other than a few decent chances for each team. That was playing in the Flyers’ favor, as they just needed to bleed the clock down against the Rangers, who had yet to have a comeback win this season. It was the Rangers who got what they needed. On the power play following a soft call on Denver Barkey, Pavel Dorofeyev tied the game at 2 with just over 6 minutes to play. Moments later, they took the lead, courtesy of Kartye. Philly pulled Woll late, giving the Flyers the extra attacker with 1:17 remaining. However, they were unable to score. That brought the game to its 3-2 final.
